title: ContextHub middleware: request telemetry orchestrator and lightweight carrier
creator: Maya Patel
description: Introduce a minimal 'ContextHub' carrier and middleware layer across language SDKs that centralizes request telemetry (trace ids, sampling decision, route metadata) with a low-overhead encoding and clear forward/backward compatibility rules. This ticket covers the core runtime hooks, carrier format, per-language middleware integration points, test harness, and an initial canary rollout plan. The goal is reliable cross-service correlation for Redwood's tracing and latency dashboards while keeping per-request CPU + alloc overhead < 0.2ms on typical customer workloads.
acceptance_criteria: ContextHub carrier spec published in Confluence (fields, versioning, header names) and linked from SDKs
Middleware implemented for Python, Node, and Go SDKs that can extract and inject the ContextHub carrier and respect sampling decisions
End-to-end trace propagation verified across a 3-service call path in the staging environment (hosted API -> dedicated pool -> private connector) with correct trace_ids and sampling flags preserved
Unit and integration tests added to each SDK repo; fuzz tests validate header truncation / unknown-version handling
Load test result: p95 CPU overhead for extraction+injection < 0.2ms and extra allocations < 1.5KB per request on benchmark harness
Console dashboard shows propagated attributes (route, model_variant) and correlates with existing trace IDs for 99% of sampled requests in canary namespace
Rollout plan documented: canary (internal traffic) -> 10% external -> 50% -> 100% with rollback hooks and observability playbook
implementation_steps: Draft ContextHub carrier v1 spec (trace_id, span_id, sampling, version, optional route tag) and decide header format (compact binary vs base64 JSON)
Prototype middleware for Python SDK using existing request hook API; measure overhead with microbenchmarks
Implement middleware in Node and Go SDKs with similar public API surface and language idioms
Add feature flag gating in SDKs to enable ContextHub header emission for canary namespaces
Create integration test harness using staging services and tracer sink to validate end-to-end propagation
Run perf regression tests and iterate on encoding/alloc strategy if p95 target not met
Open cross-functional review with security/compliance for header content and leakage risk
Prepare PRs and CHANGELOG entries, coordinate rollout with infra and console teams
notes: Decision log: opted for compact base64-encoded JSON (v1) instead of custom binary to simplify language portability; revisit v2 for binary-efficient encoding if perf shows benefits
Trade-off: including route/model metadata in carrier increases header size but avoids a 2nd RPC to enrich traces; route tag is optional and only emitted behind a flag
Interoperability: carriers must gracefully accept unknown fields and unknown versions; SDKs will ignore unrecognized keys to avoid breaking upgrades

Security: header may contain low-sensitivity metadata only; no PII allowed. Security review flagged header leak risk to third-party upstreams—we will strip ContextHub header when propagating to external partners unless allowlist enabled
Related work: reuse the request affinity token in runtime for batching decisions but keep that out of carrier v1 to reduce coupling
Perf note: initial Python implementation used dict->json->b64 which caused 0.45ms overhead at p95; switching to lightweight struct packing + pre-allocated buffer reduced to 0.12ms
Edge cases: websocket upgrade paths and async worker queues need a serialized carrier representation; design includes a separate 'queue' key for persistent sinks
Next steps: prepare Confluence spec and run a 48-hour canary on internal traffic to collect real workload latency impact
qa_checklist: Automated unit tests for extraction/injection across SDKs
Integration test that asserts sampling flag is honored end-to-end
Perf benchmark entry in CI with baseline comparison
Manual exploratory test for header stripping when proxying to external hosts
